headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs to Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, thereby protecting residential ratepayers from these infrastructure costs.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Urges Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger is advocating for data centers to cover the costs of new transmission infrastructure, aiming to prevent these expenses from being passed on to families and small businesses. This stance reflects a broader concern about the impact of data center energy demands on utility bills and grid affordability.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water users providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed, increasing transparency for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Disclosure
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that water usage by data centers be made public, aiming to provide greater transparency. This legislation is a response to growing concerns about the significant water consumption of these facilities.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Delegate Thomas.
news_headline: Virginia Residents Alarmed by Data Center Noise
news_summary: Residents in Virginia's 'Data Center Alley' are increasingly complaining about excessive noise and fumes from data centers, particularly from backup generators. This issue has led to calls for stricter regulations on data center operations and siting to protect community quality of life.
